config.enabled.name: Enable SDV-Radiance
config.enabled.tooltip: Master switch for the whole post-processing pipeline.
config.preset.hint: Tip: presets and your saved custom looks live in the on-screen tuner (open with the tuner hotkey, default F6). It previews live and always stays in sync.
config.preset.name: Quick preset
config.preset.tooltip: Apply a ready-made look. This overwrites the bloom and color-grading settings below; reopen the menu to see the updated values.
config.togglekey.name: Toggle effects on/off
config.togglekey.tooltip: Instantly turn the whole post-processing stack on or off (quick A/B compare while playing).
config.tunerkey.name: Open live tuner
config.tunerkey.tooltip: Open the on-screen tuner overlay to adjust the look while seeing the scene live.
tuner.title: SDV-Radiance Tuner
tuner.hint: Drag = preview  •  wheel = scroll  •  right-click a look = delete  •  Esc = save
config.bloom.enabled.name: Enable bloom
config.bloom.enabled.tooltip: Glow around bright areas such as lamps and sunlight.
config.bloom.threshold.name: Bloom threshold
config.bloom.intensity.name: Bloom intensity
config.colorgrade.enabled.name: Enable color grading
config.colorgrade.enabled.tooltip: Cinematic tone/palette adjustment (done in linear color space).
config.colorgrade.auto.name: Auto mood (time / weather / season)
config.colorgrade.auto.tooltip: Automatically shift warmth and saturation: warm at sunset, cool at night, cooler and desaturated in rain/snow, with a seasonal bias.
config.colorgrade.strength.name: Strength
config.colorgrade.contrast.name: Contrast
config.colorgrade.saturation.name: Saturation
config.colorgrade.temperature.name: Temperature (warm / cool)
config.colorgrade.temperature.tooltip: Negative = cooler/bluer, positive = warmer/oranger. Added on top of the auto mood.
config.colorgrade.brightness.name: Brightness
config.colorgrade.tonemap.name: Filmic tone mapping (ACES)
config.colorgrade.tonemap.tooltip: Off by default. The frame is already low-dynamic-range, so this mainly helps when Brightness is pushed above 1 — otherwise it can look muddy.
config.colorgrade.bluelight.name: Blue-light filter
config.colorgrade.bluelight.tooltip: Eye-comfort warm shift: cuts blue and lifts red a touch, like a night-light mode. 0 = off. Works even with color grading turned off.
help.lutamount: How much of the chosen look to mix in. 0 is off; the look is laid over the grading sliders, not swapped in for them.
config.colorgrade.lut.name: Look (colour LUT)
config.colorgrade.lut.tooltip: A finished look laid over the grading sliders, not instead of them. Every look here keeps black black: the game draws 12% of its pixels pure black, and 70% of a night interior, so anything that lifted the shadows would turn a dark room grey. Drop your own 1024x32 LUT strip in radiance-luts, beside your save games, and it is listed here as yours the next time the game starts. That folder is yours rather than the mod's, so updating the mod cannot delete it.
config.colorgrade.lutamount.name: Look strength
config.colorgrade.lutamount.tooltip: How much of the look to apply. 0 is off.
config.godrays.enabled.name: Enable god rays
config.godrays.enabled.tooltip: Shafts of light spreading out from LAMPS, torches and fires, strongest in a dark room or after dusk. Shafts from the sun are the separate switch below, and each works without the other.
config.godrays.intensity.name: Intensity
config.godrays.threshold.name: Light threshold
config.godrays.density.name: Ray length
config.fog.enabled.name: Enable day fog
config.fog.enabled.tooltip: Drifting screen-space mist during the day; fades out over dusk.
config.fog.nightmist.name: Enable night mist
config.fog.nightmist.tooltip: Sparse blue wisps that drift by after dusk (outdoors, clear weather). Fades in as day fog fades out.
config.fog.nightmistdensity.name: Night mist intensity
config.fog.nightmistcoverage.name: Night mist amount
config.fog.nightmistspeed.name: Night mist drift speed
config.fog.coverage.name: Fog amount
config.fog.coverage.tooltip: How much of the screen the wisps occupy.
config.fog.density.tooltip: How strongly each wisp tints the scene.
config.fog.density.name: Density
config.fog.scale.name: Mist scale
config.fog.speed.name: Drift speed
help.windowreflectionstrength: How plainly a window returns whoever stands in front of it while there is daylight behind you and a dark room behind the glass.
help.windowreflectionnight: The same after dusk, when the window is lit from inside and mostly shows the room through. Set it to 0 for glass that stops reflecting once it lights up.
help.windowsheen: How much sky a window holds when nobody is walking past it: a faint wash of the sky’s own colour, brighter at the top, and two diagonal streaks across the pane. 0 leaves the glass exactly as the map painted it.
help.windowglare: A soft blot of light that travels across a pane as you walk past it, the way a real window catches the sky. 0 turns it off.
help.windowscene: The ground and buildings in front of a window show faintly in it, squashed into the pane the way an upright mirror shows a street. 0 turns it off.
help.windowlightglow: Lamps stand in the windows facing them, each a soft blot of its own colour that fades as the lamp gets further from the pane. Brightest after dark, dimmed at midday exactly as the mod dims the pools lamps cast on the ground. 0 turns it off.
config.lighting.windowreflectionstrength: How plainly a window returns whoever stands in front of it by day. It multiplies a built-in ladder, so a mirror stays stronger than plain glass and plain glass stronger than a house window whatever this is set to.
config.lighting.windowreflectionnight.to: The strength after dusk, eased in on the same ramp the window glow rides. Lower than the daytime figure because a lit pane shows the room through it; 0 turns the image off once the window lights up.
config.lighting.windowsheen.name: Sky in the glass
config.lighting.windowsheen.tooltip: How much sky the glass itself holds, with or without anyone in front of it: a faint wash of the sky’s colour over the pane, more of it near the top, and two diagonal streaks laid at the same angle on every window in town. It fades after dusk, when the pane is lit from inside. 0 leaves the glass exactly as the map painted it.
config.lighting.windowglare.name: Glare on the glass
config.lighting.windowglare.tooltip: A soft blot of light travelling across a pane as it crosses the screen, which is what tells the eye a window is glass rather than a picture of one. It has no edges and no direction, so it never argues with the highlights your window art already has painted on. It fades after dusk with the rest of the daytime glass. 0 turns it off.
config.lighting.windowscene.name: The street in the glass
config.lighting.windowscene.tooltip: How brightly the world in front of a window stands in its glass: six tiles of ground and whatever is built on it, squashed into the pane and turned over, the way an upright mirror shows what is near it along the bottom and what is far from it higher up. It reads the same sprite-free map picture the water reflection uses, so it costs a strip of an image the mod is already making. Trees, people and animals are not in that picture; people are reflected separately. 0 turns it off.
config.lighting.windowlightglow.name: Lamps in the glass
config.lighting.windowlightglow.tooltip: How brightly the lamps of the street stand in a window. Each light in the location leaves a soft blot of its own colour in the panes facing it, fading with distance, and a window never returns its own glow. It follows the same daylight ramp the mod dims lamp pools on the ground with, so it is brightest after dark and a third of that at midday, and a lantern carried at noon shows in the glass it passes. 0 turns it off.
tuner.waterhere.always: Water here: always on (outdoor / level water)
config.tiltshift.enabled.name: Enable tilt-shift
config.tiltshift.enabled.tooltip: Keep a sharp band across the middle and blur the top and bottom (fake miniature / depth-of-field look).
config.tiltshift.mode.name: Focus shape
config.tiltshift.mode.tooltip: Bands = sharp middle strip, blurred top & bottom. Radial = sharp circle around the player, blurred outward.
config.tiltshift.radius.name: Sharp circle size (radial)
config.tiltshift.radius.tooltip: Radial mode only: how big the in-focus circle around the player is before it blurs outward.
config.tiltshift.feather.name: Edge softness
config.tiltshift.feather.tooltip: How gradually the image eases from sharp to blurred. Higher is softer, removing the hard band edge.
config.tiltshift.strength.name: Blur strength
config.tiltshift.top.name: Top blur amount
config.tiltshift.bottom.name: Bottom blur amount
config.cloudshadow.hidevanilla.name: Hide vanilla cloud shadows
config.cloudshadow.hidevanilla.tooltip: Remove the base game's drifting Cloud-critter shadows (so only this mod's cloud shadows show).
config.cloudshadow.enabled.name: Enable cloud shadows
config.cloudshadow.enabled.tooltip: Soft shadows of drifting clouds moving across the ground (outdoors only).
config.cloudshadow.opacity.name: Opacity
config.cloudshadow.coverage.name: Coverage
config.cloudshadow.scale.name: Cloud size
config.cloudshadow.count.name: Cloud count
config.cloudshadow.count.tooltip: How many separate cloud banks share the screen - low = a few big drifting banks, high = many small puffs.
config.cloudshadow.speed.name: Drift speed
config.water.enabled.name: Enable water shimmer
config.water.enabled.tooltip: Gentle refraction ripple and sparkle applied only to water tiles (the game already animates the water, so this is subtle). Experimental.
config.water.strength.name: Ripple strength
config.water.speed.name: Ripple speed
config.water.sparkle.name: Sparkle
config.water.sparkledensity.name: Sparkle amount
config.water.sparkledensity.tooltip: How many glints dot the water (their size follows along). 1.0 = the original dense look; lower = calmer surface.
config.water.caustics.name: Caustics
config.water.caustics.tooltip: The wobbling net of focused light on the bed of shallow water, strongest along the shore. Fades out at night and in bad weather.
config.water.causticsstrength.name: Caustics strength
config.water.reflection.name: Water reflection
config.water.reflection.tooltip: Faintly mirror the scene just above the surface down onto the water for a wet, reflective sheen. Subtle by design. Experimental.
config.water.reflectstrength.name: Reflection strength
config.water.indoors.name: Water effect indoors
config.water.indoors.tooltip: Apply the water effect inside building interiors (farmhouse, cabins, house mods). Turn off if a house/interior mod has decorative water you don't want rippling. Real level water always keeps the effect: caves, mines, the sewer, and the bathhouse hot spring.
config.vignette.enabled.name: Enable vignette
config.vignette.enabled.tooltip: Darken the screen edges for a cinematic frame.
config.vignette.strength.name: Vignette strength
config.ca.enabled.name: Enable chromatic aberration
config.ca.enabled.tooltip: Subtle color fringing toward the edges, like a camera lens. Keep it low on pixel art.
config.ca.strength.name: Aberration strength
config.lighting.flood.name: Flood GI lighting
config.lighting.flood.tooltip: Occlusion-aware global illumination: real light sources and skylight flood across the map tile-by-tile, so canopies and buildings cast soft shade, lamps pool warm coloured light around corners, and windows spill light at night. Replaces the classic dynamic lighting below when enabled.
config.lighting.floodstrength.name: Flood lighting strength
config.lighting.floodstrength.tooltip: How strongly the flood lightmap shades the scene. Lower keeps the vanilla look with a hint of shading.
config.lighting.floodshadow.name: Per-light shadow strength
config.lighting.floodshadow.tooltip: How dark it gets where a wall, tree, or character blocks a lamp's light. Every light source casts its own soft shadows.
config.lighting.enabled.name: Enable dynamic lighting
config.lighting.enabled.tooltip: Darken flat/unlit areas and pool warm light around real light sources (lamps, torches, fireplaces). Makes dark places read dark and lit places read bright, with soft falloff.
config.lighting.indoor.name: Indoor darkness
config.lighting.indoor.tooltip: How much to darken interiors. The game leaves most rooms flat and fully bright; this brings back shadow so lamps actually matter. 0 = off.
config.lighting.night.name: Extra night darkness
config.lighting.night.tooltip: How dark the world gets after nightfall, outdoors and in rooms we light ourselves. The moonlit ground leans cool and quiet while lamps and fires keep their full colour, so deeper night also means the lights matter more.
config.lighting.morning.name: Morning darkness
config.lighting.morning.tooltip: How much of the night darkening carries into the early morning (before 7:00). 0 = the room is bright when you wake; higher = darker mornings.
config.lighting.warmth.name: Light warmth
config.lighting.boost.name: Light brightness
config.lighting.radius.name: Light radius scale
config.lighting.shadows.name: Cast shadows
config.lighting.shadows.tooltip: Tall/solid tiles (walls, structures) block light and cast soft shadows away from each light source. Experimental.
config.lighting.shadowstrength.name: Shadow strength
config.lighting.windoweffects.name: Window daylight and glow
config.lighting.windoweffects.tooltip: Everything this mod does with windows, in one switch: daylight coming into a room, and the warm glow on house windows outdoors after dark. Turn it off if another mod handles your windows. Rooms still darken and brighten through the day either way.
config.lighting.windowbeam.name: Window beam and glass
config.lighting.windowbeam.tooltip: The part of window daylight you can see: lit glass, a beam leaning with the sun, and the patch of sun it lays on the floor. Turn this off if another window mod already draws these. The room still fills with daylight from its windows either way: that half is lighting rather than art, and a mod painting window pictures cannot do it for you.
config.lighting.windowreflection.name: Reflections in windows
config.lighting.windowreflection.tooltip: People walking past a window show in its glass. Glass reflects when what is behind it is darker than what is in front, so the image is plain by day and thins to a suggestion after dusk, as the window lights up from inside. Mirrors reflect fully, plain glass a third, house windows a fifth. Outdoors only for now.
config.shadows.enabled.name: Enable directional shadows
config.shadows.enabled.tooltip: Cast a soft, sheared silhouette of each character away from the sun, leaning by time of day (outdoors, daytime, clear weather only). Experimental.
config.shadows.strength.name: Shadow strength
config.shadows.length.name: Shadow length
config.shadows.blur.name: Edge softness
config.shadows.objects.name: Shadows for trees & bushes
config.shadows.objects.tooltip: Also cast leaning shadows from trees and bushes, not just characters.
config.shadows.leanclarity.name: Lean clarity
config.shadows.leanclarity.tooltip: Squeeze the shadow of a very small caster across the sun so that its lean is what you read. A seedling's whole shadow is a few pixels wide, so its own width hides the angle even though its tip points the same way as everything else. Only sprites a single tile or smaller are touched: stumps, crops, bushes and trees are left as they are. 0 turns it off.
config.shadows.casts.name: Shadows per character
config.shadows.casts.tooltip: How many lights a character casts a shadow from indoors and after dark, nearest first. Also a performance setting: each one is a full shadow drawn for that character, so 1 costs a third of 3 in a room full of lamps. The sun outdoors is one light and is not affected.
config.shadows.perkind.title: Length per kind
config.shadows.perkind.tooltip: How far each kind of thing's shadow may reach, as a fraction of its own height. The Shadow length slider above multiplies all of them.
config.shadows.length.trees.name: Trees
config.shadows.length.smalltrees.name: Saplings & stumps
config.shadows.length.bushes.name: Bushes
config.shadows.length.crops.name: Crops
config.shadows.length.grass.name: Grass
config.shadows.length.objects.name: Forage, fences & machines
config.shadows.softness.title: Softness per kind
config.shadows.softness.tooltip: How soft each kind's shadow edge is, as a multiplier on Edge softness above. Short shadows usually want more of it than tall ones.
config.shadows.softness.trees.name: Trees
config.shadows.softness.smalltrees.name: Saplings & stumps
config.shadows.softness.bushes.name: Bushes
config.shadows.softness.crops.name: Crops
config.shadows.softness.grass.name: Grass
config.shadows.softness.objects.name: Forage, fences & machines
config.shadows.lean.title: Lean per kind
config.shadows.lean.tooltip: How far each kind's shadow leans, as a fraction of the sun's own angle. 1 is the sun, and everything defaults to it. Below 1 a shadow is shorter and more upright, sitting closer to the base of the thing casting it, which is how crops looked before 1.5.4. The cost is that a caster set below 1 no longer points where the sun says, so it and the people beside it disagree.
config.shadows.lean.trees.name: Trees
config.shadows.lean.smalltrees.name: Saplings & stumps
config.shadows.lean.bushes.name: Bushes
config.shadows.lean.crops.name: Crops
config.shadows.lean.grass.name: Grass
config.shadows.lean.objects.name: Forage, fences & machines
config.shadows.heightdrop.name: Building & ledge shadows
config.shadows.heightdrop.tooltip: Project ground shadows from walls, buildings, and ledges (requires the Height Framework mod).
config.shadows.heightlength.name: Building shadow length
config.camera.mode.name: Camera mode
config.camera.mode.tooltip: Off = vanilla snap. Smooth = ease toward the player while moving, snap crisply when you stop.
config.smoothcam.speed.name: Follow speed
config.smoothcam.speed.tooltip: Smooth mode only. How quickly the camera catches up while moving. Lower = smoother/more trailing; 1.0 = instant.
config.renderscale.name: Effect resolution
config.renderscale.tooltip: Resolution the effects are computed at, as a fraction of your window. The game world is always drawn at full size; only the effects use a smaller image, so lowering this costs much less GPU work (0.5 is about a quarter). 1.0 = native. 0.5 is the cleanest lower setting for pixel art; values in between are softer and can shimmer slightly while the camera moves.
config.renderscaleauto.name: Lower it automatically when needed
config.renderscaleauto.tooltip: Lets the mod drop the effect resolution by itself when your frame rate is not keeping up, and put it back when the scene gets easier. The slider above stays the ceiling: this only ever asks for less than you chose, never more. It moves one step at a time and only after the frame has been slow for a while, so it does not flicker. If a step down does not actually make the frame shorter, it is given back and the mod stops trying for a minute, because then something other than the effects is the bottleneck.
help.renderscaleauto: Drops the effect resolution when frames are slow, and gives it back when they are not. The slider above is the ceiling.
config.rendersharpness.name: Upscale sharpening
config.rendersharpness.tooltip: How much sharpening is applied while scaling the effects back up to your window. 0 turns it off, 1 is the tuned default (it already gets stronger as you lower the effect resolution), and higher is crisper still. Has no effect at 1.0 effect resolution, because nothing is being scaled up.
tuner.desc.looks: Pick a ready-made look, or save your own.
tuner.desc.perf: How much work the effects do. Lower it if the game stutters.
tuner.desc.colorgrade: The overall colour of the picture: warmth, contrast, richness.
tuner.desc.bloom: Bright things glow and bleed a little light into what is around them.
tuner.desc.lens: Camera-lens touches: blurred edges, darkened corners, colour fringing.
tuner.desc.lighting: How dark rooms and nights get, and how lamps pool light.
tuner.desc.windows: Daylight through the glass, the glow after dusk, and the people reflected in it by day.
tuner.desc.shadows: Shadows cast by people, animals and objects, following the sun.
tuner.desc.godrays: Visible shafts of light, from lamps and fires or slanting down from the sun.
tuner.desc.water: Ripples, sparkle and reflections on every water surface.
tuner.desc.cloudshadow: Cloud shadows drifting slowly across the ground outdoors.
tuner.desc.fog: Daytime fog and the thin mist that gathers at night.
tuner.desc.camera: How the camera follows you as you walk.
tuner.desc.debug: Troubleshooting only. Leave this off unless you are reporting a problem.
tuner.perfhud: Show the cost readout on screen
help.perfhud: Shows what each part of this mod costs, updating as you play, in the corner of the screen. The top line is your whole frame rate, not this mod's share of it. Useful for finding the exact spot where the game stutters. It also warns you when the game window has lost focus, which by itself makes the frame rate look much worse than it is.
help.gputime: Adds a second column showing what the graphics card spends, next to what the game spends asking it. Some effects are cheap to ask for and expensive to draw, so the two can differ a lot. Off by default because it talks to the graphics driver directly; if anything goes wrong it switches itself off rather than retrying.
config.debug.name: Debug logging
config.debug.tooltip: Log render-pipeline info to the SMAPI console to help troubleshoot.
config.report.name: Write a diagnostic report
config.report.tooltip: Writes everything needed to diagnose what you are looking at right now: your version, where you are standing, the time and weather, every setting, and the mods installed. It goes to a file AND into the SMAPI log, so on a phone, where there is no console and no file you can easily reach, you can still upload the log and share the link. Stand where the problem is before you tick it. It untocks itself straight away, which is normal.
config.wip.text:
These effects are planned but not implemented yet, so they have no settings here:
- High-quality texture upscaling
Each effect will get its own options as it lands.
help.waterreflectdistort: How much the water is allowed to bend what it reflects. At 0 the reflection is a flat mirror, exactly like the reflection of a person, which has never moved. The water itself keeps rippling and sparkling either way: this is the image in it, not the surface, so ripple strength stays a separate control.
config.water.reflectdistort.name: Reflection distortion
config.water.reflectdistort.tooltip: Scales everything that bends the reflection: both the sideways shear from the wave and the displacement from the ripple. 0 is a flat mirror whichever reflection look is chosen, 1 is that look as designed. Independent of ripple strength, so calming the reflection never means flattening the water.
help.waterreflectbanding: How tall a band of the reflection moves as one when the water ripples. At 0 the reflection bends smoothly. Higher values move the reflection in steps, which is the drawn pixel-art look, and also what slices a reflected building into horizontal strips sliding over each other. 4 is what this mod looked like up to 1.5.6.
config.water.reflectbanding.name: Reflection banding
config.water.reflectbanding.tooltip: How tall a band of the reflection shares one sideways shift as the water ripples, in pixels. 0 shears every row on its own, so the reflection bends instead of breaking into strips. 4 is the look this mod shipped with up to 1.5.6.
help.waterreflectblur: How soft the reflection is. 1 is the softness this mod ships with, 0 is crisp, 2 is twice as hazy. It moves the reflected scenery and the reflected people together, so they stay one surface.
config.water.reflectblur.name: Reflection softness
config.water.reflectblur.tooltip: Scales how much the reflection is softened with depth. 1 is exactly the look this mod shipped with, so nothing changes until you move it; 0 is a single crisp sample; 2 is twice the spread. Reflected people follow the same setting as the reflected scenery.
config.water.reflstyle.name: Reflection look
config.water.reflstyle.tooltip: How much the water's own movement is allowed to break up what it is reflecting. Still water keeps the surface rippling but the image in it readable; Choppy breaks it up and reads deeper. This is separate from the ripple strength, so calming a reflection no longer means flattening the water.
help.reflstyle.still: The surface keeps rippling, but the reflection in it barely moves and sits lighter, so you can read what is being reflected. Useful in rain, where the game makes the water half again as choppy on its own.
help.reflstyle.natural: The reflection moves with the surface, which is what this mod has always shipped.
help.reflstyle.choppy: The reflection is broken up by the water and reads deeper. For open sea and weather.
tuner.windowcompat: Off: another window mod is drawing its own beam.
//: Plain-language notes shown when the pointer rests on a control in the on-screen tuner.
help.master: Turns every effect in this mod on or off at once. Nothing here touches your save.
help.colorgrade: Changes the colours of the whole picture: contrast, how strong colours are, and whether the light reads warm or cool. Off by default, so what you see is the game's own colour.
help.automood: Lets the colour settings drift with the time of day and the weather instead of staying fixed.
help.contrast: How far apart the darks and the brights are. Above 1 deepens shadows and brightens highlights; below 1 flattens the picture.
help.saturation: How strong the colours are. 0 is black and white, 1 is unchanged, above 1 is more vivid.
help.temperature: Warm or cool. To the right the picture goes orange, like late afternoon; to the left it goes blue, like an overcast day.
help.tonemap: Rolls the very brightest areas off gently instead of letting them clip to flat white.
help.bluelight: Takes some blue out of the picture, the way a night-time screen filter does. Meant for comfort, not for looks.
help.bloom: Bright things bleed a soft glow into what is around them, the way a lamp does through a camera lens.
help.bloomthreshold: How bright a pixel has to be before it starts to glow. Raise it if too much of the screen is glowing.
help.shadows: Every character, tree and object casts a shadow of its own shape, leaning away from the sun.
help.shadowlength: How far a shadow reaches. The sun's height still decides it, so shadows are long at dawn and short at noon whatever you set here.
help.shadowblur: How soft the edge of a shadow is. 0 is a hard edge; higher is a fuzzy one, like an overcast day.
help.shadowcasts: How many nearby lamps may each throw their own shadow of one character at night. More lamps means more shadows and more work for your machine.
help.shadowobjects: Whether trees, fences, crops and furniture cast shadows too, or only people and animals.
help.shadowleanclarity: Makes the tiniest shadows, on seeds and saplings, show which way they lean. Anything bigger than one tile is left alone, because its shadow is already a shape you can read.
help.shadowlean: How far a shadow leans away from what is casting it. Lower it and shadows sit closer to their own base instead of stretching out sideways.
help.lighting: The night and indoor lighting: how dark a room gets and how lamps light it back up.
help.lightindoor: How dark a room is when nothing is lighting it. Higher is darker.
help.lightmorning: How much of the night's darkness is still in the room when you wake. Vanilla mornings start fully lit; raise this for a room that brightens as the sun comes up, drop it to zero to wake in full daylight.
help.lightnight: How dark the night is, outdoors and in. Deeper night is cooler and quieter, and makes every lamp and fire count for more.
help.lightwarmth: How orange lamplight is. At 0 a lamp is white; to the right it reads like a candle.
help.lightboost: How bright each lamp burns. This is the one to raise if the night is too dark to walk in.
help.lightradius: How wide a pool of light each lamp throws.
help.lightshadows: Whether the light from a lamp is blocked by walls and furniture instead of passing through them.
help.floodgi: Bounced light. Light that lands on a floor or a wall spills onto what is beside it, so a lit corner lifts the whole area a little. GI is the usual name for this.
help.floodstrength: How far bounced light spreads. This is the contrast between a lit part of a room and an unlit one, not the overall brightness.
help.floodshadow: How dark the areas that bounced light cannot reach become.
help.windoweffects: Daylight coming in through windows: the glow on the glass and the light it throws into the room.
help.windowbeam: The visible shaft of light on the floor under a window. Turned off on its own if another window mod is drawing one.
help.windowreflection: People walking past a window show in its glass: plainly by day, faintly after dusk once the window is lit from inside.
help.godrays: Shafts of light spreading out from LAMPS, torches and fires. Off by default. A dark room or a lamplit street at night is where to look. Sun shafts are the separate switch below.
help.godraysthreshold: How bright something has to be before it throws rays. Lower it if nothing is casting any; raise it if pale walls and snow are.
help.godraysdensity: How solid the lamp shafts look, and how far the sun's dapple stretches from the trees that cast it.
help.cloudshadow: Shadows of clouds drifting across the ground on a sunny day.
help.cloudcoverage: How much of the ground is under a cloud at any moment.
help.cloudcount: Few big clouds or many small ones.
help.fog: Drifting mist over the world. Heaviest in the early morning and in the right weather.
help.fognightmist: A separate, thinner mist that comes out after dark.
help.water: Everything the mod does to water: movement, sparkle, and reflections.
help.waterstrength: How strongly the surface moves. Lower it if the ripple is distracting.
help.watersparkle: The glints of light on the surface.
help.watercaustics: The net of focused light on the bed of shallow water.
help.waterreflection: Water mirrors what stands beside it. Only what is on your screen can be reflected, so something far off the top of the screen has nothing to mirror yet.
help.waterindoors: Whether indoor water, such as a tub or a fish tank, gets the effect too.
help.tiltshift: Blurs the top and bottom of the screen and keeps the middle sharp, which makes the world look like a small model. Turn it off for an evenly sharp picture.
help.tiltfeather: How gradually the blur comes on at the edge of the sharp area.
help.tilttop: How much of the top of the screen is blurred.
help.tiltbottom: How much of the bottom of the screen is blurred.
help.vignette: Darkens the corners of the screen, the way a camera lens does, so the eye settles in the middle.
help.ca: Splits colour slightly apart towards the corners of the screen, the way a real lens does. The middle of the screen is never affected. Aberration is the camera term for it.
config.godrays.sun.name: Sun shafts
config.godrays.sun.tooltip: Sunlight falling on the ground where a canopy lets it through: bright banded patches leaning with the time of day, cut by trees and buildings, gone under an overcast sky. This is dappled light on the ground, not a beam hanging in the air - denser and hazier on a foggy morning, otherwise mostly a brightening of what it lands on. Forests and treelines show it best; open ground is lit evenly and shows none. Independent of the lamp shafts switch.
help.godrayssun: Sunlight falling through gaps in a canopy, as dappled patches ON THE GROUND rather than a beam hanging in the air. Leans with the time of day and gets denser in fog. Look at a forest floor or a treeline; open ground is lit evenly and shows none. Works on its own, without the lamp switch.
config.particles.enabled.name: Enable particles
config.particles.enabled.tooltip: Small things drifting, rising and glowing in the world itself: blossom on the wind, dust in a sunbeam, sparks over a hearth. They are drawn into the world rather than over it, so they take the light, the weather and the colour grading like everything else on the map. Off until you ask for it, because it puts things on screen that were never there.
config.particles.density.name: How many, overall
config.particles.density.tooltip: The amount for everything at once. Each kind below has its own amount which multiplies this one, so this is the single dial that turns all of them down together. Lower it first if the frame rate suffers; the ceiling on how many can exist at once does not move.
tuner.desc.particles: Blossom, dust and sparks drifting through the world
help.particles: Small things living in the world itself: petals on the wind, dust in a sunbeam, sparks over a fire. They are drawn into the scene, not on top of it, so they are lit and graded with everything else.
help.particledensity: The amount for everything at once. Each kind has its own amount below this, which multiplies it. Lower this first if the frame rate suffers.
config.particles.dust.name: Dust in the daylight
config.particles.dust.tooltip: Specks hanging in the light that comes through a window, drifting the way dust does in a beam. Indoors only, and only while a window is actually lit: outdoors the sun shafts carry motes of their own.
help.particledust: Specks hanging in the light through a window, indoors, while the window is lit. Stand in a farmhouse in the morning and look at the patch of light on the boards.
config.particles.amount.name: How much
config.particles.amount.tooltip: How much of this one there is, against the amount it carries on its own. It multiplies the overall amount above rather than replacing it, so the top slider still turns everything down at once. 0 is the same as switching it off, but it fades out instead of stopping.
config.particles.size.name: How big
config.particles.size.tooltip: How big one piece of it is, against its own size.
help.particleamount: How much of this one there is. It multiplies the overall amount at the top of the tab, so that slider still turns everything down at once.
help.particlesize: How big one piece of it is.
config.particles.embers.name: Sparks over a fire
config.particles.embers.tooltip: Sparks rising off anything the game treats as a flame: a hearth, a brazier, a torch, a wall sconce. They are added on top of the lighting rather than drawn under it, so a spark is the fire's own light and not something the room lights up. Outdoors they sink into daylight the way lamp pools do.
help.particleembers: Sparks rising off a hearth, a brazier or a torch. Stand by the saloon fireplace after dark. Outdoors they fade into daylight the way lamps do.
config.particles.fireflies.name: Fireflies
config.particles.fireflies.tooltip: Fireflies over a field on a summer night, on top of the ones the game flies itself. When they fly is the game's own rule rather than one of ours, so a field never has two opinions about whether it is a firefly night.
help.particlefireflies: Fireflies over a field on a summer night, added to the ones the game already flies. Stand outdoors in summer after dark.
config.particles.petals.name: Blossom and leaves
config.particles.petals.tooltip: Petals on the wind in spring, leaves in summer and autumn, outdoors. The game only puts anything in the air on a Wind day, so an ordinary spring afternoon has nothing blowing through it at all: that is the gap this fills. On the days the game does run its own, this drops to a quarter and moves on the game's wind rather than a wind of its own, so the two blow together. None in winter or in rain.
help.particlepetals: Petals in spring, leaves in summer and autumn, drifting outdoors even on days the game leaves the air empty. It thins out on the game's own windy days rather than doubling them.
config.particles.ringsparkles.name: Sparks around a glow ring
config.particles.ringsparkles.tooltip: Pale sparks turning slowly around a player wearing a glow ring, so the light it casts has somewhere visible to have come from. They stay where they were made rather than following you, so standing still they turn around you and walking they trail out behind.
help.particleringsparkles: Pale sparks turning around you while a glow ring is worn. Wear one and stand still, then walk: they are left behind rather than carried along.
config.godrays.sunintensity.name: Sun shaft strength
config.godrays.sunintensity.tooltip: How strong the sunlight through a canopy is. Its own dial rather than the lamp rays', because the two share a word and nothing else: a lamp ray is a streak drawn out of a bright pixel at night, a sun shaft is daylight cut by the trees it comes through.
config.godrays.sunreach.name: Sun shaft reach
config.godrays.sunreach.tooltip: How far the dappled light stretches from the canopy that cuts it. Higher is longer patches reaching further into the open.
help.godrayssunintensity: How strong the sunlight through a canopy is, on its own dial rather than the lamp rays'. The two only share a word: one is a night-time streak off a lamp, the other is daylight cut by trees.
help.godrayssunreach: How far the dappled patches stretch from the trees that cut them. Higher reaches further into the open ground.
tuner.desc.weather: Rain and snow drawn by this mod instead of the game: layered streaks that lean with the wind and splash where they land, and snow that falls as flakes instead of a scrolling texture.
config.precipitation.enabled.name: Radiance rain & snow
config.precipitation.enabled.tooltip: Draw precipitation ourselves instead of letting the game draw it. Rain becomes three planes of wind-blown streaks with splashes; snow becomes drifting flakes. Off, the game's own rain and snow are untouched.
config.precipitation.rain.name: Rain
config.precipitation.rain.tooltip: Replace the rain. Green rain is replaced too: the same streaks shifted lime and reading heavier, with the sheet's own green splashes.
config.precipitation.snow.name: Snow
config.precipitation.density.name: Amount
config.precipitation.density.tooltip: How much is in the air, against the amount the weather brings on its own.
help.precipitation: Draw rain and snow ourselves instead of letting the game draw them. Rain becomes layered streaks that lean with the wind and splash where they land; snow becomes drifting flakes. Storms rain harder on their own.
help.precipitationrain: Replace the rain drawing. Green rain is replaced too, in its own sickly lime.
help.precipitationsnow: Replace the snow drawing: drifting flakes in three sizes instead of the game's scrolling texture.
help.precipitationdensity: How much is in the air, against the amount the weather brings on its own.
config.lightning.name: Lightning response
config.lightning.tooltip: The scene answers a lightning strike: shadows kick toward the bolt for a blink, this mod's own darkening lifts with the game's flash, and a short warm afterglow follows. With the game's screen-flash accessibility option off, the visible parts stay off and only a reduced scene response remains.
help.lightning: For a blink after each strike, shadows lean toward one direction as if the bolt were the sun, the mod's darkening lifts with the game's own flash, and a short warm afterglow follows. Works with vanilla rain too; the replacement rain is not required.
config.wetworld.lensdrops.name: Drops on the screen edge
config.wetworld.lensdrops.tooltip: A few drops clinging to the edges of the screen while it rains, frost in a snowfall - never the middle of the picture. Gone shortly after the weather stops.
help.wetworldlensdrops: A few drops on the edges of the screen while it rains, frost while it snows. Never the middle of the picture.
config.lightningbolts.name: Visible bolts
config.lightningbolts.tooltip: Draw a bolt in the sky with the flash, on any map. The game only ever shows one on the farm, and only when a lightning rod or a crop was actually hit; everywhere else a storm is a white screen and a sound. Uses the game's own bolt art.
help.lightningbolts: A bolt in the sky with the flash, on any map, drawn with the game's own bolt art. Not every rumble gets one: some strikes stay behind the clouds.
config.precipitation.wind.name: Windblown leaves
config.precipitation.wind.tooltip: Replace the wind-day debris: blossom in spring, leaves in summer and autumn, white flecks in winter, in three depth layers that tumble and ride the wind instead of the game's flat fluttering chunks.
help.precipitationwind: On windy days the game blows flat fluttering chunks across the screen. This replaces them with blossom or leaves in three depth layers that tumble, flutter and ride the same wind the rain leans with. The colours follow the season wherever you stand.
config.precipitation.size.name: Size
config.precipitation.size.tooltip: How big one piece is, against its own size.
config.precipitation.opacity.name: Visibility
config.precipitation.opacity.tooltip: How strongly it shows. Amount, size and visibility are three different answers to three different complaints: too few, too small, too faint.
help.precipitationsize: How big one piece is, against its own size.
help.precipitationopacity: How strongly it shows, apart from how much of it there is.
config.wetworld.lensdropsize.name: Drop size
config.wetworld.lensdropsize.tooltip: How big the drops on the glass are, against their own size.
config.wetworld.edgehaze.name: Misted edge
config.wetworld.edgehaze.tooltip: The breath of condensation along the screen edge while it rains, and the frost creeping in from the corners while it snows. Zero leaves clear glass around the drops.
help.wetworldlensdropsize: How big the drops on the glass are, against their own size.
help.wetworldedgehaze: Condensation along the screen edge in rain, frost creeping in from the corners in snow. Zero leaves the glass clear around the drops.
help.cloudscale: How large one drifting cloud shadow is. Larger means fewer, broader banks of shade.
help.fogscale: How large one wisp of mist is. Larger means broader, slower shapes.
config.godrays.decay.name: Ray length
config.godrays.decay.tooltip: How far a ray reaches before it dies out. Lower is a short stub at the light itself, higher is a long streak across the screen. One value shapes the lamp streaks and the sunlight through a canopy alike, because both are drawn by the same pass.
help.godraysdecay: How far a ray reaches before it fades out. Low is a short stub at the light, high is a long streak. It shapes the lamp rays and the sun shafts together.
config.fog.topbias.name: Thicker toward the top
config.fog.topbias.tooltip: How much thicker the fog is at the top of the screen than at the bottom. 0 is even across the picture; 1 is twice as thick up there, which reads as fog lying in the distance rather than around your feet. Day fog and night mist are one pass, so this shapes both.
help.fogtopbias: How much thicker the fog is at the top of the screen than at the bottom. 0 is even, 1 is twice as thick up there, which reads as distance. It shapes the day fog and the night mist together.
config.water.rainringdensity.name: How many rings
config.water.rainringdensity.tooltip: How many places on the surface a drop strikes, against the number the weather brings on its own. Below 1 fewer places take their turn; above it every one of them does and the pattern tightens. 0 leaves the water unbroken in the rain.
config.water.rainringsize.name: Ring size
config.water.rainringsize.tooltip: How wide one ring grows before it dies. The wall of the ring grows with it, so a large one still reads as water moving rather than as a drawn circle.
config.water.rainringstrength.name: How plainly they show
config.water.rainringstrength.tooltip: How brightly the rings and the point each drop lands on stand out from the water. Apart from how many there are and how big they get.
help.waterrainringdensity: How many places a drop strikes the surface. 0 leaves the water unbroken in the rain; above 1 the pattern tightens.
help.waterrainringsize: How wide one ring grows before it dies.
help.waterrainringstrength: How brightly the rings stand out, apart from how many there are and how big they get.
config.water.reflectdepth.name: Reflection depth
config.water.reflectdepth.tooltip: How far a reflection reaches down into the water before it fades into sky. Higher suits open water, where a cliff or a stand of trees really is that tall; lower suits a stream a tile or two across, where the mirrored bank runs on for more water than there is. 1 is the shipped depth and about 0.55 is what 1.5.3 used.
config.water.reflectreach.name: Reflection reach
config.water.reflectreach.tooltip: How much of the scene is allowed to reflect at all. Lower it and things far from the water stop being mirrored, which is the cheapest way to make reflections affordable without turning them off.
help.reflectdepth: How far down into the water a reflection carries before it turns to sky. Turn it down if reflections in a narrow stream reach further than the stream is wide.
help.reflectreach: How much of the scene reflects at all. Lower costs less and mirrors fewer things.
